senses.gloss: f.(also pl.) (συνέδριον) Sanhedrin, the supreme council of the Jews; ס׳ גדולה the Great S., consisting of seventy-one members; ס׳ קטנה the Small S., a judicial court of twenty-three.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 1:6">Ib.</cite> <he>ראויה לס׳</he> fit to be a seat of the S.
<cite ref="Mishnah Makkot 1:10">Macc. I, 10</cite> <he>ס׳ נוהגת בארץ וכ׳</he> the S. may exercise its functions in Palestine and outside.

<cite ref="Mishnah Makkot 1:10">Ib.</cite> <he>ס׳ ההורגת וכ׳</he> a S. that executes capital punishment (more than) once in seven years. Ib. 9 (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 17:6">Deut. XVII, 6</cite>) <he>שלא תהא ס׳ שומעת וכ׳</he> this intimates that the S. must not hear the testimony from the mouth of an interpreter.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 63a:23">Snh. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>לס׳ שהרגו וכ׳</he> that a S. which puts a person to death must not taste food during the entire day of execution; a. v. fr.—Pl. <he>סַנְהֶדְרָיוֹת</he>, <he>סַנְהֶדְרָאוֹת</he>, <he>סַנֶּדְרָ׳</he>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 1:5">Ib. I, 5</cite> <he>אין עושין ס׳ לשבטים וכ׳</he> supreme courts for tribes (provincial courts, Small Sanhedrin) can be instituted only by decree of the court of seventy-one; Sifra K’dosh. ch. VIII, Par. 10 <he>סנדריות של ישראל</he>; Yalk. Lev. 619 <he>סנהד׳ של שבטים</he>, opp. <he>ס׳ גדולה</he>.
Snh. 16ᵇ כנדראות (also in Chald. diction); a. fr.—Sanhedrin, name of a treatise, of the Order of N’ziḳin, of Mishnah, Toseftaand Talmud Babli a. Y’rushalmi.
